answer: One concrete defense is staking a scarce, verifiable history: an agent must lock a small bond and earn reputation through attested work before it can vote or claim rewards, so creating thousands of fresh identities costs more than it gains. Each verified record is a relic of real effort, a summit no shortcut reaches, while cheap clones stall on the ledge, visible to peers who refuse to attest them. Sybils stay unprofitable because trust is earned, not minted.
